item.title: U.S. Hunger Leverages Amazon Quick and Spaces for Data‑Driven Food Assistance
item.description:
U.S. Hunger Leverages Amazon Quick and Spaces for Data‑Driven Food Assistance

U.S. Hunger has adopted Amazon Quick and its Spaces capability to bring real‑time data insight to its food‑assistance operations.

🔍 Overview

  • Delivered more than 250 million meals.
  • Historically reached 59 countries, now focused primarily on the United States.
  • Reported ~500 % growth over four years while headcount grew only 15–20 %.
  • President and CEO Rick Whitted spent 30 years in banking before leading the organization.

🛠️ How Quick and Spaces Work

  • Quick extracts data from a SQL Server into its in‑memory engine SPICE via nightly refresh jobs at 2 AM ET.
  • Data originates from Impact Manager, the organization’s proprietary cloud‑based platform, and from the Full Cart program that delivers donor‑funded food to households.
  • Spaces provide a shared workspace where colleagues can store documents, definitions, and analyses for a specific business area.
  • Shared definitions of KPIs ensure everyone agrees on metric meanings.
  • A leadership‑wide KPI document was built over more than a year across NetSuite, Salesforce, Impact Manager, and the payroll system.
  • The technology team and a research data colleague prepare datasets and supply definitions to help the CEO interpret information.

📊 Impact on Operations

  • 17 colleagues across executive leadership, technology, Full Cart, finance, compliance, and support have access to Quick.
  • In Quick, the CEO can comment directly on drafts, regenerate reports with incorporated changes, and refine instructions without moving between Word and chat.
  • Chat serves as the CEO’s primary day‑to‑day AI workspace, while Spaces is the most used capability.
  • Using a Space with Salesforce call reports, the CEO drafts instructions on measures, data sources, and definitions for the technology team.
  • Quick provides a live connection to how leadership thinks through problems, allowing others to pick up where the CEO left off in a financial model or KPI framing without scheduling another meeting.

👥 Leadership & Collaboration

  • The organization first learned about Quick at an AWS Social Entrepreneur Accelerator event led by Kat Esser.
  • CTO Ezekiel Brooks enabled access to core Full Cart datasets for the CEO.
  • Rick Whitted remarked, “The families we serve today, their stories are my story.”
  • He also said, “With all the knowledge and data we have, Space reduces as much noise as possible and narrows my discussion.”
  • The financial Space is shared with the CTO, COO, and finance leadership, granting access to tools and business context behind analyses.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Shared definitions and live data reduce reliance on meetings and manual document handling.
  • The combined Quick + Spaces workflow lets the organization scale its impact efficiently while maintaining data‑driven decision‑making.
  • By grounding financial and operational insight in the real stories of families, U.S. Hunger aligns its rapid growth with its mission.

#AWS #DataAnalytics #NonprofitTech #FoodAssistance

Source: How U.S. Hunger connects leaders and data using Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services

item.title: ONE Data Launches Development Finance Observatory AI Platform
item.description:
ONE Data Launches Development Finance Observatory AI Platform

ONE Data, an initiative of the ONE Campaign, launched the Development Finance Observatory on October 14, 2026 during the World Bank‑IMF Annual Meetings. The AI platform is supported by The Rockefeller Foundation and Google.org and aims to give free, rapid access to global aid, lending and debt data.

🔍 Overview

  • The Development Finance Observatory is an AI‑powered data analyst that brings together fragmented development finance data in one place.
  • It is described as “a world‑class data analyst in your pocket.”
  • The platform is built on Google’s Data Commons and supported by the Rockefeller Foundation’s independent charitable affiliate RF Catalytic Capital (RFCC).

🧩 How it works

  • The platform unifies isolated datasets—from the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, Organisation for Economic Co‑operation and Development, and other sources—into a single AI‑ready foundation.
  • Users can query the data with natural‑language questions instead of navigating raw spreadsheets, turning analyses that previously took months into minutes.
  • Every number is traceable to a specific source, preventing AI‑hallucinations.
  • Calculations and visualizations that used to take months now take minutes.

⚙️ Key details

  • Launch date: October 14, 2026, Washington, D.C.
  • Funding: $4 million in combined funding from ONE Data, Google.org and The Rockefeller Foundation (announced in January).
  • Technology partner: Built on Data Commons by Google with support from RFCC.
  • Initiative: Part of ONE Data, which “transforms fragmented, inaccessible development data into trusted, actionable insights for policymakers, campaigners, journalists, and citizens.”

🚀 Availability

  • The platform is publicly available, offering free, rapid access to aid, lending and debt data for governments, journalists, think tanks and the public.
  • Users can ask natural‑language questions and receive answers in seconds with confidence that the answers are correct.

💡 Why it matters

  • The observatory gives leaders a clearer picture of aid, debt, private capital and other financial flows, enabling faster, smarter decisions about where limited resources can have the greatest impact.
  • As the development finance landscape is “being rewritten in real time,” transparent, accountable data is essential for building a more effective system.
  • Quotes from stakeholders:

    “We believe policy makers — who make decisions that impact millions of people’s lives– deserve world class insights.” said David McNair, Managing Director of ONE Data. “We built the Development Finance Observatory so that policymakers, journalists and citizens can get the answers they need in seconds — with the confidence that those answers are right. “Data Commons was built so organizations like ONE can focus on solving the world’s biggest challenges without worrying about data storage and APIs,” Prem Ramaswami, Head of Google Data Commons, said. “The development finance landscape is being rewritten in real time, and we cannot build a better system without understanding how money is actually moving,” said Mike Muldoon, Chief Executive Officer of RFCC, The Rockefeller Foundation’s independent charitable affiliate.

#developmentfinance #AI #dataanalytics #publicpolicy

Source: ONE Data Launches AI Platform That Transforms International Development Sector

item.title: Using Agents to Rewrite Apache Spark User-Defined Functions for GPU Acceleration
item.description:
Using Agents to Rewrite Apache Spark User-Defined Functions for GPU Acceleration

Agentic AI and demanding enterprise applications are compounding the need for vast amounts of data and frequent, complex queries. To meet this demand, NVIDIA cuDF is utilizing agents to automate the rewriting of Apache Spark User-Defined Functions (UDFs) into GPU-accelerated code, achieving speedups of over 22x.

🔍 Overview

  • Enterprise applications require greater data throughput without a proportional increase in cost.
  • NVIDIA cuDF addresses this by leveraging the massive parallelism and high-bandwidth memory of GPUs for data analytics.
  • The NVIDIA cuDF plugin for Apache Spark brings this acceleration to the industry-leading platform for big data processing.
  • While the plugin transparently parallelizes row-wise operations using Spark’s declarative interface, UDFs break this abstraction by containing opaque user code.

🧩 How it works

During standard execution, UDFs force the GPU accelerator to convert data from columnar to row-wise format and fall back to the CPU to execute code row-by-row. This introduces round-trip data transfer overhead and forgoes compute speedup.

By using agents, developers can now rewrite these UDFs into GPU-accelerable forms within minutes. This automation replaces a laborious engineering process that requires careful API selection, semantic validation, and performance measurement.

⚙️ Key details

Method Description
Spark SQL Expression Replaces simple UDFs with equivalent expressions visible in Spark’s expression tree for GPU replacement during query planning.
RapidsUDF Interface Allows UDFs to operate directly on GPU-resident ColumnVectors using the Java API for cuDF operations.
Custom CUDA Kernels Invoked through the Java Native Interface (JNI) for highly complex logic that cannot be composed from existing operations.

💡 Why it matters

  • Performance: Rewriting UDFs eliminates the overhead associated with accelerator fallback, yielding speedups of over 20x.
  • Efficiency: Automated rewrites by coding agents reduce the significant engineering effort previously required for manual vectorized programming.
  • Cost: The cuDF plugin enables better TCO performance in major enterprise workloads by increasing throughput without proportional cost increases.

#NVIDIA #ApacheSpark #AIagents #GPU #DataAnalytics

Source: How to Rewrite Apache Spark UDFs for GPU Acceleration with AI Agents | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: MarketBeat launches company news sentiment scoring system
item.description:
MarketBeat launches company news sentiment scoring system

MarketBeat has introduced a sentiment scoring system that assigns a numeric rating to each news headline and aggregates those ratings into company‑level sentiment scores.

🔍 Overview

  • Each headline receives a score ranging from 2 (good news) to -2 (bad news).
  • Scores are averaged over the most recent 7 days to produce a company news sentiment score.
  • The system tracks headlines from hundreds of news outlets and tags them by company.

⚙️ How it works

  • Headlines are collected in real time from more than one hundred trusted media outlets.
  • A numeric score is assigned to each headline according to its perceived tone.
  • The platform calculates the average sentiment for each company based on the scores from the last seven days.
  • A separate chart compares the number of articles about a company in the last seven days with the average weekly article count.

📊 Current sentiment highlights

  • PNC News Sentiment: ▼ 0.19
  • PRHI News Sentiment: ▼ 0.88
  • SAFE News Sentiment: ▼ -0.08
  • GRND News Sentiment: ▼ 0.46
  • Average Finance News Sentiment: ▲ 0.63

📈 Why it matters

  • The sentiment scores help investors identify companies receiving positive press versus those under negative coverage.
  • By showing article volume trends, the tool highlights changes in media attention that may precede market movements.

🚀 Availability

  • The sentiment data is available through MarketBeat’s platform, which also offers a free daily newsletter for the latest news and ratings on companies and their competitors.
  • Users can subscribe via the website or receive SMS alerts (available in multiple countries) that include stock alerts, news stories, and partner offers.

#NewsSentiment #Finance #DataAnalytics #MarketBeat

item.title: 🤖 Democratizing Data Science: How Amazon Q Developer is Revolutionizing Machine Learning for Everyone
item.description:
🤖 Democratizing Data Science: How Amazon Q Developer is Revolutionizing Machine Learning for Everyone

𝙎𝙪𝙢𝙢𝙖𝙧𝙮: Amazon Q Developer in SageMaker Canvas transforms ML model creation from a weeks-long expert task into a natural language conversation. This AI agent system lets non-technical users build sophisticated machine learning models in minutes through simple dialogue, automatically handling data preparation, model selection, and optimization while providing transparency into the entire process.

🚀 The Machine Learning Revolution Just Got More Accessible

Machine learning has traditionally stood behind a wall of technical expertise. Building predictive models typically requires specialized knowledge in data science, machine learning algorithms, and a thorough understanding of business contexts. Even for experts, the process from data acquisition to model deployment can stretch across days or weeks.

But what if you could simply ask for the machine learning model you need?

That’s exactly what Amazon Q Developer in SageMaker Canvas delivers. Generally available since February 28, 2025 (after its beta preview at re:Invent 2024), this generative-AI-powered assistant lets anyone build and deploy sophisticated machine learning models through natural language conversation—no ML expertise required.

📸 See illustration above showing the chatbot interface of Amazon Q Developer for SageMaker Canvas

🧠 How Amazon Q Developer Works: AI Agency in Action

At its core, Amazon Q Developer functions as an 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺—an autonomous AI that acts on your behalf. Here’s the fascinating part: the system combines a large language model (LLM) interface with a structured nonvolatile-memory block that retains critical information throughout your conversation.

The workflow begins with you describing your business problem in plain language. For example, you might say: “I’m a credit risk analyst at a bank and want to classify loan applicants as default or non-default based on their financial characteristics and economic indicators.”

From there, you can:

  • Select an existing dataset
  • Create a new dataset from S3, Redshift, SQL, or Snowflake
  • Simply upload a CSV file from your computer

The system expects tabular data with target columns (what you want to predict) and feature columns (data points used for prediction). For time-series forecasting, you’ll also need a timestamp column.

📸 See illustration showing the architecture of Q Developer data science assistant

What makes this system truly powerful is its dependency graph structure—each node represents a problem variable like problem_type, evaluation_metric, or target_column. This architecture helps the agent infer missing variables necessary for building your ML model.

🔍 Automatic Intelligence: From Data to Predictions

Once you’ve provided your dataset and described your problem, Amazon Q Developer takes over with remarkable autonomy:

🧹 Intelligent Data Preparation

The system automatically:

  • Cleans data and fills missing values
  • Encodes categorical features
  • Handles outliers
  • Removes duplicate rows/columns

Throughout this process, you can ask follow-up questions about your dataset (e.g., “What percentage of rows have missing values?” or “Are there outliers?”) and use DataWrangler for advanced analytics and visualization.

🤖 Sophisticated Model Building

Amazon Q Developer doesn’t just build a single machine learning model—it creates an 𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗹𝗲 of models including XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, linear models, and neural networks.

The system automatically:

  • Identifies the appropriate ML task type (classification, regression, or forecasting)
  • Suggests appropriate loss functions based on your needs
  • Conducts hyperparameter optimization (HPO)
  • Manages feature engineering

All of these complex processes are handled behind the scenes, without requiring any technical input from you.

📸 See illustration showing dataset analysis with Q Developer in SageMaker Canvas

📊 Transparent Results and Deployment

After training, you can:

  • Run inference on test datasets
  • Deploy your model as a SageMaker inference endpoint in just a few clicks
  • Access an automatically generated explainability report

The explainability report is particularly valuable, offering visualizations and insights into:

  • Dataset properties
  • Feature attribution scores (which variables matter most)
  • The model training process
  • Performance metrics

💡 Why This Matters: The Democratization of ML

The significance of Amazon Q Developer extends far beyond convenience. This tool represents a fundamental shift in who can access the power of machine learning:

  1. Breaking down technical barriers: Business analysts, domain experts, and other non-technical professionals can now leverage advanced ML without waiting for data science teams.

  2. Accelerating development cycles: What once took weeks can now be accomplished in minutes or hours.

  3. Maintaining quality: By using ensemble methods and automatic optimization, the system often achieves performance comparable to models built by experienced data scientists.

  4. Preserving transparency: Unlike many AI systems, Q Developer provides clear explanations about model decisions and feature importance.

For organizations looking to become more data-driven, this technology offers a path to widespread ML adoption without massive investments in specialized talent or extended development timelines.

🔮 The Future of Human-AI Collaboration in Data Science

Amazon Q Developer represents an early glimpse into a future where AI agents work alongside humans, handling the technical complexities while humans focus on problem definition and business insights.

Rather than replacing data scientists, tools like this expand the ecosystem, allowing experts to focus on more complex challenges while empowering non-specialists to solve predictive problems independently.

As these systems evolve, we can expect even more intuitive interfaces, better automated feature engineering, and deeper integration with business intelligence systems—ultimately making ML as accessible as spreadsheet formulas are today.

Ready to transform your data into powerful ML models without extensive data science expertise? Start exploring Amazon Q Developer in SageMaker Canvas today and experience the simplicity of building ML models using natural-language commands.

What business problem could you solve with a conversational ML assistant at your fingertips? 🤔
